on the veranda is empty now.
of how long since Father left the chair
to hang upon the wall as a photograph.
Now that chair is still there,
in that corner of the upstairs balcony;
dust has gathered, rust has taken hold.
though seeing things, could not see,
he sat silently staring into emptiness.
When the doctor came, he smiled at him,
the pills lying on the little table,
You know, don't you, he has Alzheimer's!

we did not listen to him.
under the pretence of hearing something,
We ourselves devised new definitions of life
a new chautisha of self-interest and relationships.
perhaps this is how a household goes awry,

before.label: English
before.title: Why, After All—the Sting of Not Belonging
stanzas: tormented by the sting of not belonging.
the courtyard where I was born,
the house where I grew up—
how can it be someone else's??
At the age for playing, reading and writing,
I was taught the ways of housekeeping.
my dream was scorched to ashes.
a grave injustice was done to me.
In the name of giving away a daughter,
a vow I was made to memorise.
is the new house not my own??
In my parents' home I was another's wealth;
why this sting of not belonging??
